central_invariant: The local-only mock broker runs in an independent non-root Docker container with no network, read-only root and zero capabilities. Only the broker container mounts its synthetic secret and durable SQLite private directory, never the isolated worker. The worker can only access the signed public grant and Unix socket. Kernel SO_PEERCRED, signed frozen scope and first-use SQLite claim still gate all mock admissions.
broker_image: locally built from same pinned Python base, cryptography==50.0.0, cffi==2.0.0, pycparser==2.23; exact produced image ID captured in evidence
docker_build_network: build-only PyPI dependency installation; neither runtime container has egress
private_directory: owner mode 0700; synthetic credential file 0600; persistent SQLite under broker-only mount
protected_material_in_proof: ephemeral synthetic test-only byte token; no production Provider key
trust_assumptions: Host Linux kernel and Docker daemon trusted
Host runner with Docker permissions and broker UID trusted
UID/GID credential can be imitated by same-host privileged actors
The public signed test grant is not enrolled operator authorization
The broker secret is synthetic and the sink does no Provider HTTP
The image build downloads dependencies from PyPI; dependency supply-chain independently unverified
exclusions: No full-process compromise resistance on host
No live Provider secret vault or IAM binding
No production operator key custody or trusted clock
No full AgentDojo model messages/tools authenticity
No billable API request or native bank effect
next: Independent artifact + configuration audit; then consider broker provider egress allowlist, real operator-root enrollment and full source/request binding as separate proof rounds before any real execution.
